title: Review a big Plan one checkpoint at a time
statement: As an architect I can review a large Plan's work one checkpoint at a time, seeing what was done before, what this checkpoint did, and what is to come, so no review is one huge shot
overview:
A Plan of 200 Tasks across 6 phases cannot be reviewed well at the end, in one go. A
checkpoint is a kind of phase: a few phases of work, then a checkpoint. It holds no Tasks
of its own and covers every Task since the previous checkpoint. It is where the agent takes
a breath and proves the work it did works.

## What is decided

- **Shape.** A checkpoint is a phase in the Plan's ordered phases, after the phases it covers.
- **Scope.** Its review covers what changed since the previous checkpoint merged. A reviewer
  may reach further back when they choose.
- **Proof.** Its review shows the work works: the tests and evidence behind the criteria it
  addresses.
- **Passing.** Once approved, the agent merges the checkpoint's branch into the branch the
  Plan's work comes from, usually a feature branch, and the next checkpoint starts there in a
  new workspace. Whether a checkpoint also gets a pull request with colleagues is up to the
  user. Reaching the main branch stays the feature branch's own review.
- **Who passes.** Whoever invokes the Plan decides: themselves, or the agent unless what it
  found is surprising or urgent.
- **The gate.** Tasks beyond a checkpoint that has not passed are not offered as ready, and
  starting one warns instead of refusing.
- **Size.** Explaining a checkpoint should take five or six slides, not ten to twenty. Before
  the work exists that is estimated by counting things: roughly a slide per story addressed,
  with the Tasks it holds beside it. Once the review exists, its slides are the measure.

## Surprising enough to stop

An agent allowed to pass a checkpoint still stops for a person when any of these holds:

- the work departed from the Plan: a review callout names a Task, or Tasks were added,
  dropped, or moved since the checkpoint began;
- an agent reported a Task blocked during the checkpoint;
- a test or check is failing, or a criterion the checkpoint addresses has no evidence;
- the review needs more slides than the estimate, or more than six.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Reaching a checkpoint creates a review of its branch as a change into the branch the Plan's work comes from, covering what changed since the previous checkpoint merged
A reviewer can widen a checkpoint's review to an earlier checkpoint when they choose
The checkpoint's review shows the Plan's board with work done before, work in this checkpoint, and work to come told apart
The checkpoint's review lists the stories and acceptance criteria its Tasks address
The checkpoint's review shows the tests and evidence behind each criterion it addresses, and names any criterion with none
